cls: Recombinant growth factor - epidermal growth factor (wound-healing biologic)
quick: Topical/intralesional preparations vary by product - e.g., topical rhEGF gel/spray applied to the ulcer; intralesional rhEGF (e.g., 75 microgram) into/around the ulcer 3 times weekly
Not applicable - applied to wounds (topical or intralesional)
Safety not established; use only if clearly needed
No systemic dose adjustment defined (local application)
No systemic dose adjustment defined (local application)
Wound healing, local infection, injection-site reactions (intralesional product)
summary: Recombinant human epidermal growth factor (rhEGF) is a biologic that stimulates the proliferation of epidermal and other cells to promote wound healing. It is used, depending on the product, as a topical gel/solution or by intralesional injection to accelerate granulation and closure of difficult wounds such as diabetic foot ulcers and burns. It is approved in several countries (e.g., as Heberprot-P intralesional, or Easyef topical) but is not FDA-approved.
indications: Adjunctive treatment of hard-to-heal wounds, particularly diabetic foot ulcers (intralesional rhEGF)
Promotion of healing of burns, skin-graft donor sites, and chronic wounds (topical rhEGF), per the specific product

dosage.d: e.g., 75 microgram rhEGF infiltrated into/around the ulcer (per Heberprot-P)
dosage.n: Continue until granulation/closure (commonly up to 8 weeks); reconstitute and use per product

dosage.d: Apply rhEGF gel/solution to the cleaned wound surface (per product, e.g., Easyef)
dosage.n: After wound cleansing/debridement; cover with dressing

admin: Use only on the wound as directed - this is not a systemic medicine
Clean/debride the wound before application as instructed by the product
For intralesional products, infiltrate into the wound bed and edges using aseptic technique
For topical products, apply a thin layer to the wound surface and cover with an appropriate dressing
Follow the manufacturer's reconstitution, storage, and treatment-duration instructions
moa: Recombinant human epidermal growth factor binds the EGF receptor (EGFR) on keratinocytes, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells, triggering tyrosine-kinase signaling that stimulates cell proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix formation. This accelerates granulation tissue growth and re-epithelialization, promoting wound closure.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to rhEGF or excipients
Known or suspected malignancy at or near the treatment site (growth-factor stimulation concern)
relative: Severe peripheral ischemia of the limb (optimize perfusion)

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; use only if the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: Safety during breastfeeding has not been established; use with caution. Systemic absorption from local application is expected to be low.
renal: No systemic dose adjustment is defined for local (topical/intralesional) use.
hepatic: No systemic dose adjustment is defined for local (topical/intralesional) use.

moderate: Theoretical concern with concurrent use over a known/occult malignancy (growth-factor stimulation)
minor: No significant systemic drug interactions reported with local use

common: Local pain or burning at the wound/injection site
rare: Theoretical promotion of pre-existing malignant cells

monitoring: Wound size and granulation/epithelialization at each visit
Signs of local or systemic infection
Glycemic and vascular optimization in diabetic foot ulcers
counsel: This is a wound treatment applied directly to the ulcer - it is not taken by mouth
Keep the wound clean and follow the dressing and follow-up schedule exactly
Continue good diabetes control and foot care, and offload pressure from the ulcer
Report increasing pain, redness, discharge, fever, or worsening of the wound
Treatment is continued for a set number of weeks - keep all appointments
pk: Local cellular stimulation begins promptly; visible granulation improves over days to weeks
Local tissue effect; minimal systemic exposure
EGF is rapidly cleared systemically (minutes); action is local
Repeated applications/injections over weeks until wound closure
Store refrigerated at 2-8 C (per product); do not freeze; reconstitute immediately before use
pearls: Used mainly for hard-to-heal diabetic foot ulcers - intralesional rhEGF (Heberprot-P) reduces amputation in some studies; topical rhEGF (e.g., Easyef) is used for wounds/burns
Always combine with standard wound care: debridement, infection control, offloading, and glycemic/vascular optimization
Avoid applying over a known or suspected tumor because EGF stimulates cell proliferation
NOTE: rhEGF is a biologic approved in various countries but NOT FDA-approved; dosing/indication follow the specific product's prescribing information
missed: For a missed scheduled application or injection, perform it as soon as practical and resume the regular schedule; do not double up. Maintaining the treatment schedule supports continued healing.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with local use. Excess local application/injection might increase local reactions (pain, inflammation). There is no specific antidote; manage symptomatically and resume the recommended dosing.
